title: Find the open tickets that describe something broken, blocking or unsafe, so nothing important is lost
description:
## As asked

**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour) and JKershaw/simple-dispatcher (their tickets share one Linear team).

**What this is for.** There are about 1,358 open tickets, two-thirds of them older than five weeks. John: "A large backlog isn't actually a problem as long as we're not losing important things in the mix. A lot of it can be consolidated, or will be overtaken/made redundant. Trying to figure it all out in advance will be a fool's errand \[typed "a good errand"; John confirmed the reading\], but tackled in chunks will likely help." This is the one pass over everything. The rest is sorted in chunks alongside the work.

**What we want.** One pass over every open ticket that finds those describing something broken, something blocking work, or something touching safety (security or authority included), noting for each whether it still looks true. Nothing is closed, moved or changed in this pass.

**Done when** this ticket carries the list, noting for each whether it still looks true, and no other ticket has been touched.

**Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** One read-only pass over every open ticket, listing each broken, blocking or unsafe one with whether it still looks true; neither Survey finds anything this ask needs to work, so ranking, duplicates and tooling stay out.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implementation Plan

**Implemented as approved; no deviations in approach.** The read-only pass over every open ticket was run as planned: frozen inventory of 1,366 tickets (snapshot 2026-11-10T07:54:56Z), result in 18 comment parts on this ticket (1,281 claim rows over 888 tickets; 478 tickets with no claim), plus two annex comments restoring the untrimmed evidence of 95 trimmed rows and a corrections comment, added at close-out on the review's request. There is no repository change or PR, as planned. Review verdict: Approve, conditional on the annex and corrections, which close-out discharged.

The full plan, its revisions and the decisions list are preserved in the task snapshots (archived before this prune) and in the comment trail; the close-out summary comment `## Close-out — LIN-4400` records the final state and the accepted limits.

fits one session

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4400 @ b315e0e8f

(LinearViewer `origin/main` b315e0e8f; simple-dispatcher read at 5d8489e7f.)

**Why this will be hard**

1. **Volume.** There are 1,363 open tickets (1,073 Backlog, 286 Todo, 4 In Progress), with 4.05M characters of description between them. Comments need a separate fetch per ticket at 60/min, about 23 minutes of calls. So "one pass" really means chunks plus a merge, and some proof that every ID was covered.

2. **Cheap filters don't work.** Only 123 carry `Bug`. Keywords match 74%, and "token" can mean CSS, LLM or credential. 47% are machine-filed `kind:follow-up` or `kind:review-residue`, which often mention a breakage under a neutral title. Classifying means reading.

3. **"Still looks true" is the costly half.** 533 cite `file:line` in older code. 1,175 refer to a ticket that is now Done. Only 23 have a commit on main that leads with their ID, and none of the Bug-labelled ones do. Spot checks:
   - **LIN-676** (OpenRouter OAuth CSRF): `routes/openrouter-auth.js` is now PKCE with the verifier in the session, still with no `state` parameter. Whether that closes the hole is a security call, not a grep.
   - **LIN-1740**: `followup.js:55` and `abort.js:85` still reject `'no-session'` using local state. That's only a defect if more than one instance is deployed, which code can't tell you.
   - **LIN-1101**: the root cause is in `mangodb`, outside both repos.

4. **A previous pass exists.** The "backlog-wide bug review" on 2026-08-03 left triage notes. Reuse them.

5. **The `Duplicate` state is a blind spot.** 51 tickets sit in a `duplicate`-type state, outside the ~1,358. Two are Urgent safety or wedge items (LIN-1898, LIN-1808). LIN-1898's canonical, LIN-1899, is Done, so that one is fine. But a duplicate whose canonical closed without covering it is exactly the "lost" case.

**Deeper:** half the open set is residue from the close-out leftover rule. While that rule runs, this list starts going stale the day it lands, so it should record the date of its snapshot.

**What I'd do first**

1. **Freeze the snapshot.** Store the open IDs and the 51 duplicates on this ticket, so chunks can be reproduced and "every ticket" can be checked.
2. **Triage on title, labels and priority.** Sort into *not*, *maybe* and *in*. Fetch bodies and comments only for *maybe* and *in*. Always include Urgent/High, `Bug`, and anything security-like by meaning.
3. **Three verdicts, not two:** *confirmed at BASE*, *gone at BASE*, *can't tell from code* (deployment or external package).
4. **Check the 51 duplicates in one pass:** is the canonical's state right, and does it actually cover the claim?
5. **Split by ID range** across parallel readers that return structured rows. Merge into one list that names its BASE and snapshot date, posted in parts if it's too long for one comment.

Nothing here needs a ruling from John yet.

## Survey global: LIN-4400 @ b315e0e8f

(LinearViewer `origin/main` b315e0e8f; simple-dispatcher `origin/main` 5d8489e7f.)

**Where it lands.** Mostly in the tracker, not in code. It touches code in two places: the proxy it reads through, and whatever script does the reading. The first is in good shape. The second is the messy part:
- `scripts/` holds 236 files. 170 of them are `survey-*` one-offs, named by ticket, with outputs in git-ignored `data/`. Nothing inventories them: `docs/areas/areas.json` deliberately has no `scripts/` patterns.
- A paced proxy pager (`get()` with retry and backoff, plus a hard-coded `TEAM` id) has already been copied into four fetchers (`survey-repeats-fetch.mjs`, `survey-overlap-fetch.mjs`, `survey-rules-fetch.mjs`, `survey-reliability-tracker.mjs`). Eight scripts each set their own pace.
- The August "backlog-wide bug review" left no trace in either repo. It lives only on tickets.

**Done the obvious way**, this task adds a fifth pager and another fetch/analyse pair, plus a list in a comment on LIN-4400. Nothing in the code would read that list:
- Home's Up next (`lib/home-view.js`, `upNextOf`/`compareRank`) ranks by priority, then due date, then **newest first**. The comment there says why: 88 ready High tasks.
- Close-out's existing-ticket check (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, Follow-up Triage) looks at relations and search, not at a list on another ticket.

The task forbids touching other tickets, so a confirmed old High bug stays exactly where it sank. That ranking rule is the deeper cause behind the ticket: old important tickets get lost because Up next picks the newest within a priority. Size isn't what loses them.

**The other moving part**, landed 8 Nov (LIN-4371/4374/4376): `LEFTOVER_RULE` (`lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`) now routes larger in-area leftovers to `## Waiting` entries in `docs/areas/<slug>.md`, not to tickets. A clear improvement; it applies to code shape, not defects, so defects stay with tickets, which matches this task. But two notes are already at the 6,144-byte cap the guard enforces (`runs-and-dispatch.md` 6,142, `llm-and-prompts.md` 6,073). The notes can't take in old ticket residue. Don't move anything there in this pass, and don't treat a Waiting entry as proof a ticket is covered: the rule says an item never lives in both places.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry:**
- Keep the reader out of the repo (or in scratch). If it has to land, put the existing pager in one shared helper first, not a fifth copy.
- Make the output machine-joinable: one row per ticket with identifier, class (broken/blocking/safety), verdict (*confirmed at BASE* / *gone at BASE* / *can't tell from code*) and the cited path at BASE. Then the next chunked pass can diff it rather than redo it. Comments cap at 50,000 characters (`MAX_COMMENT_LENGTH`), so plan for parts.

**Better still, not this task's:**
- A ruling from John on how confirmed findings resurface: priority bumps, a `related` link to LIN-4400, or a ranking key that stops "newest first" burying old confirmed defects.
- Stopping close-out residue from refilling the backlog faster than chunked passes can drain it. The area notes are one start on that.
- A home for `scripts/` survey tooling.

[LIN-4400 result 1/18]

## LIN-4400 result: read-only pass over the open backlog

**Snapshot:** 2026-11-10T07:54:56Z (open tickets in team LinearViewer `7e6de730-3028-4ebc-af8a-a4de237a686d`). Repository pins (`git rev-parse main` on fresh GitHub clones at snapshot): LinearViewer `b315e0e8f3e1e5f3b5d6e634e53c5dc83b41d754`; simple-dispatcher `5d8489e7fd8434f0e69af7df11a3746790abbe64`. Verdicts cite these SHAs. The working-tree checkouts were not used.

**Inventory:** 1366 open tickets (state not Done, Canceled or Duplicate). 2976 tickets in Done, Canceled or Duplicate state were excluded and not examined. The survey count (1,363) is superseded.
**Coverage:** reviewed IDs = inventory exactly (1366 of 1366; 0 missing, 0 extra). 888 tickets carry at least one claim; 478 are recorded as `none`.
**Rows:** 1281 claim rows, 1019 broken, 83 blocking, 179 safety. Verdicts: 864 confirmed at BASE, 255 gone at BASE, 162 can't tell from code.

**Sample miss rate (the coverage check):** the first pass called 586 tickets `none`. A blind widened pass re-read all 586 in full; 107 of them (18.3%) carry at least one claim the first pass missed. A seeded 29-ticket sample gave 5 hits (17%). Both are above "a few percent", so the blind pass was widened to all 586 rather than trimmed. The widened pass used a broader reading of `broken` (stale doc or comment that misleads; test that is vacuous or leaves a guard unpinned). Many of its additions are of that kind. They are marked `widened pass`. Whether they count is a ruling for John (see below).

**Second read of every `gone at BASE` claim** (evidence hidden, verdict re-decided from the ticket and BASE code): 255 agree gone; 21 changed to confirmed; 4 changed to can't tell. A disagreement never stays gone. A few long comment threads (LIN-751, LIN-1408, LIN-4150) were searched by topic in the second read rather than read in full; the first pass covered them in full.

**Full reads for partly read tickets:** LIN-751 (description and all 54 comments), LIN-4150 (all 173 comments), LIN-2083, LIN-2114 and LIN-4211 were re-read in full and their rows replaced the partial ones.

**Named claims**
- LIN-676 (OAuth CSRF, session-held PKCE without `state`): safety, **can't tell from code**. The SameSite=Lax session cookie blocks a cross-site POST plant, and the exchange uses the victim's verifier. A failed exchange leaves the verifier, and Lax still sends the cookie on a cross-site top-level GET. Settle: whether OpenRouter accepts a verifier-less code, and a two-browser live run.
- LIN-1740 (`no-session` rejections): broken, **can't tell from code**. The rejections exist at `followup.js:55` and `abort.js:85`. The docs describe one supervisor per checkout, and multi-instance is a future option. Settle: how many dispatcher instances poll the same Harbour workspace token.
- LIN-1101 (`mangodb` root cause): **can't tell from code**. The failing code is in the external `@jkershaw/mangodb` package (0.1.2 pinned in LinearViewer `package-lock.json`) and in session-viewer. Settle: mangodb `readDocuments()` source and changelog at the pinned version.

**2026-08-03 backlog-wide bug review:** one note found, on LIN-1101. Its five claims were re-checked at BASE: two gone (LIN-1834 pointer; Bug label boost excluded for Backlog state), one confirmed (session-viewer defects unreachable from these repos), two can't tell (external mangodb). No other note from that review exists in the fetched comments.

**Not covered by this pass:** later-created tickets (outside the snapshot); the duplicate-state tickets, including LIN-1808 (Urgent), which were not examined.

**Recommendations, not blockers**
- Duplicate-state check: one reading of the 51 Duplicate-state tickets would close the LIN-1808 gap. Offered for John's call.
- Standard for `broken`: a ruling is needed on whether stale doc or comment and vacuous-test claims count. Either way the widened rows are kept and marked.
- Resurfacing: nothing reads this list and no ticket tracks that gap. A ranking change would be a separate ruling.

**What was and was not done:** no ticket was created, moved, edited or closed; this comment and the inventory comment are the only writes. No repository was changed; no branch or PR was opened, since the plan forbids repo changes. All tooling and intermediate files are in session scratch. The ticket fetcher used GET only.

**Parts:** this is part 1 of N. Each later part lists claim rows, one per line in the form `ID | class | verdict | claim | evidence (BASE SHA cited) | settle`. The final part lists `none` tickets and the counts.

[LIN-4400 result 2/18]
